# Results — Study 594 (Leverage Rotation, TQQQ + 200SMA)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
Reddit-famous **"Leverage for the Long Run"** plan: hold **TQQQ** (3x daily Nasdaq-100)
while **QQQ closes above its 200-day SMA**, sit in **T-bills** below, and get *"3x upside
without 3x crashes"*. TQQQ only exists since 2010, so we synthesise the 3x fund from QQQ's
daily total return (validated against real TQQQ at **corr 0.9989**) and run the rule from
QQQ's 1999 listing through the dot-com crash the marketing never shows. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete month before the 2026-07-03 run; later days are
sliced off). Fingerprint `82b00d3939c8`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **auto-adjusted (total-return)** closes: QQQ (6,869 days, 1999-03-10 → 2026-06-30), real TQQQ (2010-02-11 →), ^IRX 13-week T-bill yield (cash leg + financing rate) |
| Synthesised 3x | `r_3x = 3·r_QQQ − 2·rf − fee/252`, all-in fee **2.5%/yr** (expense ratio + swap spread, calibrated once vs real TQQQ). Audit vs real TQQQ 2010-02-12 → 2026-06-30 (4,119 days): daily corr **0.9989**, residual drag **−0.04%/yr**, RMS tracking error **18.6 bps/day**, terminal-NAV ratio **1.080** |
| Signal | QQQ close > its own 200-day SMA (first live signal **1999-12-22**) |
| Execution / lag | signal on day *t*'s close, position holds day *t+1*'s return — exactly **one** execution lag, applied once |
| Costs | one-way × full NAV per switch (a switch trades 100% of NAV once); headline **5 bps**, sweep 0/2/5/10 |
| Cash leg | T-bill accrual from ^IRX; **Sharpe races are excess-vs-excess** (both legs minus the same T-bill accrual) |
| Survivorship | none on the instrument (QQQ/TQQQ are the actual vehicles, not a survivor panel); the *strategy's fame* is itself survivor-selected — it went viral on a 2010+ window that starts after the one regime that kills it (shown below) |

## Headline race — 1999-12-22 → 2026-06-30 (26.5 years, 6,669 days, net of 5 bps)

| leg | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe (excess) | MaxDD | $1 becomes |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Rotation** (3x above 200SMA, T-bills below) | **+11.50%** | 50.9% | **+0.433** | **−95.14%** | ×17.81 |
| QQQ buy & hold | +9.00% | 26.8% | +0.384 | −82.96% | ×9.77 |
| 3x buy & hold (synthesised TQQQ) | −2.11% | 80.4% | +0.353 | −99.98% | ×0.57 |

Exposure **73.7%** of days in the market; **186 switches** (**7.0/yr** — the whipsaw count).

## Is the timing real? (the Signal axis)

| test | value |
|---|--:|
| rotation − QQQ B&H, daily mean | +4.67 bps/day, **HAC t = +1.66** (NW lags 10, n = 6,669) |
| rotation − 3x B&H, daily mean | −2.50 bps/day, HAC t = −0.61 |
| random-timer baseline (exposure **and** switch-count matched, **40 seeds**) | seed-averaged **Welch t = +0.05** (sd 0.37); real Sharpe +0.433 vs random mean +0.314; beats 78% of seeds on Sharpe; random mean CAGR −0.11% |
| mean channel (next-day QQQ, above vs below SMA) | +5.08 vs +4.18 bps/day, **Welch t = +0.14** |
| vol channel (next-day QQQ, below vs above SMA) | **40.4% vs 19.8% ann. (2.05×), Welch t = +13.79** on squared returns |

**The split verdict, on the real tape:** the 200SMA is a genuine **volatility switch** —
next-day QQQ vol below the line is 2.05× the vol above it (*t* = +13.79, far past the bar) —
but it carries **no certified return timing**: the next-day *mean* is the same on both sides
(*t* = +0.14), the CAGR edge over QQQ B&H is not distinguishable from zero (*t* = +1.66),
and against random timers holding the same exposure with the same switch count the mean edge
is exactly nothing (*t* = +0.05). What the rotation demonstrably does is *avoid variance*,
not *pick returns* — which is why it beats the 3x-forever grave (−2.11% CAGR) yet cannot
certify an edge over plain QQQ.

## Costs (one-way bps × NAV per switch) — costs are NOT the problem

| cost | CAGR | Sharpe | MaxDD |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps | +11.89% | +0.440 | −95.1% |
| 2 bps | +11.73% | +0.437 | −95.1% |
| 5 bps | +11.50% | +0.433 | −95.1% |
| 10 bps | +11.10% | +0.426 | −95.2% |

Seven switches a year on one of the most liquid ETFs alive: the 0→10 bps sweep costs 0.8 pp
of CAGR. The strategy's problem is the path, not the friction.

## SMA-window robustness (net of 5 bps)

| window | CAGR | MaxDD | switches | HAC t vs QQQ |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 150 | +10.24% | −98.6% | 220 | +1.37 |
| **200** | **+11.50%** | **−95.1%** | **186** | **+1.66** |
| 250 | +14.38% | −86.9% | 146 | +2.11 |

Only the *post-hoc best* window (250) crosses *t* = 2 — a textbook parameter-fishing
pattern, not a certification. The claimed rule is 200; the 200 tape reads +1.66.

## Sub-periods (net of 5 bps; total return / max drawdown inside the window)

| window | Rotation | QQQ B&H | 3x B&H | switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| dot-com crash 2000-03-24 → 2002-10-09 | **−91.8% (dd −92.3%)** | −82.7% (dd −83.0%) | −100.0% (dd −100.0%) | 21 |
| GFC 2007-10-31 → 2009-03-09 | −54.6% (dd −56.6%) | −52.3% (dd −53.4%) | −94.4% (dd −94.6%) | 15 |
| COVID crash 2020-02-19 → 2020-04-30 | −41.5% (dd −55.3%) | −6.5% (dd −28.6%) | −38.5% (dd −69.7%) | 4 |
| 2022 bear | −42.9% (dd −45.6%) | −32.6% (dd −34.8%) | −79.0% (dd −80.9%) | 9 |
| 2020 full year | +100.9% (dd −55.3%) | +48.4% (dd −28.6%) | +111.4% (dd −69.7%) | 4 |

Two distinct failure modes, both on the tape: **(1) the parabolic-top trap** — in 1999 QQQ
went vertical, so by the 2000-03 peak the 200SMA sat ~35% below price; a 3x holder loses
most of everything *before* the exit even fires, then 21 whipsaw switches in the 2000-02
chop grind off the rest (−91.8%, barely better than an un-levered B&H). **(2) the V-crash
whipsaw** — COVID fell too fast for a 200-day line and recovered above it too fast: the
rotation sold low, re-entered high, and turned QQQ's −6.5% window into −41.5%. The rule
shines only in the *slow* bear it was drawn for (2022: −42.9% vs 3x's −79.0%).

## Third axis — $10,000 at the 2000-03-24 QQQ peak: does the dot-com cohort survive?

| leg | trough | MaxDD | made whole | final (2026-06-30) |
|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| **Rotation** | **$507** | **−95.14%** | **2018-06-14 (18.2 yrs underwater)** | **$104,982** |
| QQQ B&H | $1,729 | −82.96% | 2015-02-13 (14.9 yrs underwater) | $75,338 |
| 3x B&H | $2 | −99.98% | **NEVER** | $3,349 |

**BUSTED.** The promise is *"3x upside without 3x crashes"*; the 2000 cohort got a
**−95% crash** — deeper and longer than plain QQQ's — and spent **18.2 years** under
water. The rotation does beat the 3x-forever grave (which ends 26 years later at a third
of the original stake) and eventually out-earns QQQ ($105k vs $75k), but only for an
investor who holds through a 95-cents-on-the-dollar loss for two decades. That is a 3x
crash by any name.

## Cross-check on the REAL TQQQ tape (2010-02-12 →, net of 5 bps)

| leg | CAGR | Sharpe | MaxDD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| rotation (real TQQQ) | +33.30% | +0.820 | −55.9% |
| QQQ B&H | +19.91% | +0.913 | −35.1% |
| TQQQ B&H (real) | +44.12% | +0.883 | −81.7% |

corr(rotation on real TQQQ, rotation on sim 3x) = **0.9992** — the synthesis is faithful
where both exist. On this bull-heavy window the rotation beats QQQ (HAC *t* = **+2.52**) —
**this is the window the Reddit backtests show**, and it begins *after* the one regime
that kills the strategy. On the same window the rotation **lagged simply holding TQQQ**
(HAC *t* = **−2.02**): post-2010, the SMA filter only *cost* money. The 2010+ *t* = 2.52
is sub-sample selection, not certification; the full-tape number is +1.66.

## Synthetic control — the machinery proof (never market evidence)

| world | seed-avg Welch t vs random timer (40 seeds) | real Sharpe vs random | mean-channel Welch t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (effect = 0, i.i.d.) | **−0.18** | +0.872 vs +0.910 | −0.67 |
| planted (persistent bear regimes, −0.8%/day) | **+3.65** | −0.208 vs −1.019 | +6.24 |

In an i.i.d. world with no trend structure the rotation does **not** beat a matched random
timer (−0.18); when persistent negative-drift regimes are planted, the same harness lights
up decisively (+3.65). The pipeline can detect real timing skill — so finding none on the
QQQ tape (*t* = +0.05) is informative, not impotence.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** *Real on the volatility channel, none on the return channel.* The
  200SMA state is a genuine vol switch (below-line vol 2.05× above-line, Welch
  *t* = **+13.79** on the real tape) — but the return timing certifies nothing: HAC
  *t* = **+1.66** vs QQQ B&H, seed-averaged Welch *t* = **+0.05** vs exposure-and-switch-
  matched random timers, mean channel *t* = +0.14. The rule avoids variance; it does not
  pick returns.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Costs are irrelevant (7 switches/yr; 0→10 bps costs 0.8 pp
  CAGR) and the vehicles are perfectly accessible — what eats it is the **path**: a
  −95.14% drawdown with 18.2 years underwater for the 2000 cohort, a fast-crash whipsaw
  that turned COVID's −6.5% into −41.5%, and a modern era (2010+) where the filter
  *significantly lagged* just holding TQQQ (*t* = −2.02). A regime-conditional
  leveraged-beta bet whose famous backtest starts after its own funeral.
- **"Does the 2000 dot-com cohort survive it?" — BUSTED.** Trough **$507 on $10,000**
  (−95.14%), made whole only in **2018**. It survives *relative to* the 3x-forever grave
  ($2 trough, never whole) — but "3x upside without 3x crashes" is exactly what the 2000
  cohort did not get.
